uncited: This family of methods initializes 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) primitives using pre-existing 3D geometry (point clouds or meshes) rather than relying solely on sparse Structure-from-Motion (SfM) outputs.
All methods in this family map input geometric primitives (vertices or points) to Gaussian centers.
The core shared mechanism is the derivation of initial covariance parameters (scale and rotation) and color features from the input geometry or associated rendering data.
**Color Initialization:** The zeroth-order spherical harmonic coefficient (`_features_dc`) is set to the RGB color of the corresponding point or rendered pixel.
**Scale Estimation:** Scales are derived from local density or depth.
**Opacity Initialization:** Opacity is initialized to a low value (e.g., raw parameter $\approx -2.197$ corresponding to 0.1) to prevent early overconfidence and allow gradient propagation .
A variant focusing on isometric spherical initialization based on depth.
The standard 3DGS initialization relies on sparse SfM points .
